Explicit HTML/document/ref, event, content, environment and installation differences remain recorded; no additional public family or runtime dependency is accepted.

mappings.api: Fixed five trigger modes, sixteen positions, controlled visibility, delayed hover, container/context selection, Foundation positioning, overflow/spacing/margin/arrow, outside/Escape/focus and close lifecycle fields. Native default trigger slot explicitly binds attrs, triggerProps and native callback refs; content and custom arrow use owned slots. Instance exposes focusTrigger, rePosition and getPopupId. No disabled prop, automatic child cloning or additional public family. TooltipTriggerProps provides optional mouse/focus/keyboard callbacks declared as Pick over common native event fields, required tabIndex and data-popupid; caller event composition invokes the internal callback and then its business callback. Trigger refs and keyed refs support only HTMLElement/null in the Tooltip creation document and realm; Element|null is the pinned JSX callback entry signature, not an SVG/MathML/component/foreign-realm compatibility promise.
mappings.types: TooltipProps, Trigger, Position, ArrowBounding, RenderContentProps and RenderContent are mapped to ./tooltip with Vue CSSProperties and native events. RenderContent is primitive-only; rich content uses TooltipSlots. TooltipInstance, TooltipTriggerScope, TooltipTriggerProps, TooltipNativeRef and TooltipPrimitive are Vue-specific subpath types. React generic RefObject/ReactNode and private state/adapter types are not exported as compatibility promises. TooltipTriggerProps onKeydown also uses common KeyboardEvent fields, while component onEscKeyDown/onClickOutSide retain complete native event types. class retains Vue HTMLAttributes class wide boundary; optional props explicitly allow undefined. initialFocusRef shares the Element|null entry signature but requires a focusable HTMLElement in that same document and realm; it does not guarantee every HTML element is focusable.
mappings.statics: Fixed __SemiComponentName__ and contextType are framework metadata, not static child components. The candidate exposes no static subcomponent or class instance state.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root provides Tooltip value only. ./tooltip provides default/named Tooltip and public types. Existing aggregate and standalone Tooltip CSS/SCSS sources are reused. Node root remains infrastructure-only; React legacy deep paths, CJS and component SSR/hydration are unsupported. The production Tooltip-only Foundation/es-toolkit inline closure is an internal package provenance profile, not a runtime dependency or public subpath.

limitations: Local source, strict declarations, production builds, full browser/documentation/E2E checks and four isolated tarball consumers establish the recorded browser contract. No publication, SSR, hydration, CJS or other public family acceptance is included.

No default trigger wrapper or React child probing/cloning. Every trigger binds native callback refs and spread props/attrs explicitly; disabled/loading trigger wrappers are caller-owned. wrapWhenSpecial does not infer React child states.

Content prop/callback returns synchronous string, number, boolean, null or undefined only. Rich content and custom arrows use native slots; showArrow is boolean. initialFocusRef is a native Element|null callback, not a React generic RefObject.
focusTrigger follows Foundation: returnFocusOnClose must be true and trigger must not be custom. Controlled notification does not guarantee the caller accepts visibility changes.

Public components require browser Vapor ESM. Node root provides infrastructure only; no CJS, component SSR or hydration support. Host creation-document and publicly accessible ShadowRoot/iframe paths retain the existing boundaries.

Vue 3.6.0-rc.9 / vue-jsx 3.3.0-rc.2 remain pinned. Strict independent compiler installation is still peer-rejected; producer precompilation and plain strict tarball declarations prove separate scopes. skipLibCheck=false remains the ordinary gate; exact call sites do not prove all dependency declarations compatible.
Pure Vapor and ordinary Vue interop are separate flows. Screenshots and current Chromium results do not establish full pixel parity, Firefox/WebKit or real device coverage.

Existing fixed Tooltip SCSS and the G06 patched Foundation source policy are reused. Production inlining allows only the pinned eighteen Tooltip/base/a11y/log and es-toolkit sources, with two full MIT notices, source hashes, exact versions and unchanged patch pin; graph/provenance/maps are checked bidirectionally, including known snapshots when claims are erased. No dependency/patch scope expansion or unrelated family acceptance is proposed.

Call-site own undefined and removed props restore initialization-time effective defaults. Global own undefined remains an explicit override; required position becoming undefined fails fast before Foundation geometry rather than silently falling back. False, zero and empty string retain field-specific semantics.

The private manually positioned portal preserves the fixed SCSS portal-inner min-width:max-content sizing on the actual inner box. Numeric geometry converts to px; wrapper style remains separate. Container origin alignment is private adapter behavior and does not change fixed upstream SCSS.

Trigger handlers publicly guarantee only common native mouse/focus/keyboard Pick fields to fit the pinned RC2 JSX namespace. Runtime forwards actual full browser events; callers compose the actual native event with internal optional handler then business callback. Public component callbacks preserve their specified full native event type.

Packed member policy permits only the fixed eighteen digest names with their original .js/.mjs extensions and the exact tooltip-inline-provenance.json name. It does not grant cross-package acceptance or production Foundation/React/lodash runtime dependencies; map and package contracts remain responsible for contents, package scope, graph and license binding.

Native ref HTML boundary: triggerRef/getTriggerRef accept creation-document, same-realm HTMLElement or null only; SVG, MathML, component handles and foreign document/realm targets are unsupported. initialFocusRef must target a suitable focusable HTML element in that document/realm. Element|null remains the JSX entry type only.

The root tsconfig, unchanged Foundation patch file, two third-party MIT notice files and technical consumer guide are reviewed auxiliary inputs. Their paths remain in the local proposal manifest rather than accepted evidence because they are outside G16 formal evidence roots. Formal scripts/profile and unit fixtures record the version/hash/license/patch checks; no source input is excused from these checks.

families.reviewedDecision: The fixed browser Popover wrapper contract is accepted over the existing Tooltip Foundation, G11 resource/event and G12 motion facilities. Native refs and owned slots replace React child cloning; synchronous primitive callbacks, exact defaults, controlled rules, native event order, geometry, focus/ARIA and teardown have explicit source and runtime evidence. Strict declarations, current live Chinese documentation/E2E and four actual isolated tarball consumer flows passed independent review. The recorded type, slot, native realm, animation/style and environment differences remain explicit; no other public family is accepted by this decision.

mappings.api: Native Vapor Popover wraps the same Tooltip Foundation, overlay and motion lifecycle. Fixed Popover defaults, card structure, arrow styling, visibility commands, notification order, focus and role rules are retained. Explicit scoped native trigger refs and owned content slots replace React child cloning; primitive synchronous content callbacks retain the Tooltip adaptation boundary. The named ArrowStyle helper is not exported; arrowStyle remains the fixed structural field of PopoverProps and ArrowProps.
mappings.types: PopoverProps and ArrowProps map fixed source inputs to readonly Vue props and native callback/slot contracts; PopoverState retains the unused upstream exported type only. Element|null JSX ref entry types require same-realm current-document HTMLElement targets. Position uses the sixteen Tooltip type/Foundation branches; Popover PropTypes lists fourteen and Chinese docs twelve.
mappings.statics: Popover has no public static child component. __SemiComponentName__ retains Popover metadata; React contextType is replaced by existing Vue context. The public instance provides focusTrigger only, with Foundation returnFocusOnClose/non-custom rules. An explicit valid call may focus its connected native trigger while its own popup remains open; it does not override a higher nested focus owner.
mappings.subpaths: The fixed upstream root exposes only the Popover value. The Vue browser root additionally exports seven type-only declarations: the three fixed component type concepts and four strict native slot/trigger/instance adaptations. ./popover exposes default/named Popover and those public types plus five shared Tooltip types. Node root remains infrastructure-only; fixed CSS/SCSS entries use the configurable theme prefix. No upstream React lib/es/lib/cjs component paths or CJS/SSR/hydration acceptance.

limitations: Complete local source, strict declarations, per-file coverage, numeric browser geometry, resource/motion/accessibility behavior, live Chinese documentation/E2E and four isolated tarball consumers establish this recorded browser contract only. Other public families remain independently reviewed; no publication, SSR, hydration, CJS or full pixel acceptance is included.

The same Tooltip primitive callback adaptation is retained; structured rich content uses the native content slot. Unsupported callback results fail without unsafe HTML conversion, with private shared resource cleanup. No title/footer/confirm/cancel API or public Arrow component is added.

Current-document, same-realm HTMLElement trigger/ref and container boundaries are retained. Disabled elements use caller-owned explicit native wrappers; no child probing/cloning, SVG/MathML/component handles or foreign-document scope expansion.

Pure Vapor, ordinary Vue interop and plain strict declarations are separate consumer flows. Pinned standalone Vue RC9/vue-jsx RC2 compiler installation remains subject to its strict peer-resolution rejection, independent of producer precompilation.

No publication, component SSR, hydration, CJS, complete pixel, cross-browser or real-device acceptance. Existing production Foundation patch and eighteen-source Tooltip inline closure and two MIT licenses are reused without expansion.

Standalone Popover styles reuse only the locked Tooltip motion keyframes and two existing runtime motion classes, with explicit source adaptation metadata; no full Tooltip visual stylesheet fallback is used.

When guardFocus is enabled, G11 also redirects programmatic outside focus; guarded portal blur settles in one scope- and layer-checked microtask before Foundation consumes it. With guardFocus disabled, zero-delay blur retains synchronous Foundation behavior.

A successful explicit focusTrigger call temporarily suspends its own guarded layer while that connected native trigger holds focus. Focus departure or relevant trigger/guard/return option, root, layer, closure or disposal changes end the exception; unrelated content/reposition updates preserve it. Custom or returnFocusOnClose=false retains the fixed Foundation no-op; a higher nested focus owner is not bypassed.

families.reviewedDecision: The complete fixed browser Collapsible contract is accepted as native Vapor with an owned default slot and private native state. Controlled defaults, measured heights, retention, final caller CSS timing, rapid reversal, zero/no-event settlement, reduced motion and teardown have explicit source, strict declarations, real browser and documentation evidence. Complete local verify, four isolated tarball consumer flows, per-source four-dimensional coverage and production audit passed independent review. React lifecycle/ref, cancellation, ARIA responsibility and environment differences remain explicit. This decision accepts only local browser Collapsible behavior; no other family, SSR, hydration, CJS, publication or pixel-parity acceptance.

limitations: Native Vapor owned default slot replaces React children; no public Foundation/state or React component lifecycle ref methods.
id is on the inner content node, as in fixed implementation, despite upstream prose.
No initial completion; disabled/reduced motion settles immediately without onMotionEnd. Zero/no-event enabled motion settles once before slot removal.
Late child/cancel events and obsolete generations cannot complete the current request. Caller final CSS timings use a finite native timer bound.
Caller owns focus, hidden/inert and ARIA; keepDOM is visual/lifecycle retention only.
Fixed RC9/RC2 strict TSX peer rejection remains. No SSR, hydration, CJS, npm publication or full pixel-equivalence claim.
Base styles also ship the exact fixed Theme animation.scss CSS variables, including upstream zero-duration/curve/delay/transform defaults; component-only use loads base before Collapsible.

mappings.api: Fixed controlled isOpen and all duration/motion/keepDOM/lazyRender/collapseHeight/adaptive/fade/reCalcKey/class/style/id/onMotionEnd fields; Vue native attrs and owned default slot; explicit cancellation/reduced/no-event differences.
mappings.types: CollapsibleProps uses Vue HTMLAttributes and synchronous CollapsibleSlots; explicit undefined restores effective defaults; private React state and Foundation internals remain private.
mappings.statics: __SemiComponentName__ and getEntryInfo preserved; no static subcomponent or imperative ref. React defaultProps/getDerivedStateFromProps are runtime adaptation internals.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root plus default/named semi-ui-vue/collapsible, paired CSS/SCSS; Node root excludes public components. No legacy React lib/es/lib/cjs mirroring.

families.reviewedDecision: The fixed browser OverflowList collapse and scroll contracts are accepted as native Vapor with real owned slot outlets, stable keyed item wrappers, temporary single-tree measurement and scoped resize, intersection, font and scheduling resources. Strict source/generated declarations, real geometry and lifecycle regressions, Chinese live examples, pure Vapor and separate Vue interop, complete local verification, per-source four-dimensional coverage and four isolated tarball consumer flows passed independent review. Renderer, slot, integer-width, event ordering, safe input, shared scroll fallback ownership and environment differences remain explicit. This decision accepts only OverflowList local browser behavior; no other family, component SSR/hydration, CJS, publication or full pixel-equivalence acceptance.

limitations: Raw render callbacks accept synchronous native content and primitive/recursive-array normalization; named slots accept only Vue VaporRenderResult/null/undefined, with text inside native JSX containers. The locked Vue JSX type union cannot statically distinguish all Vapor and VDOM values. Ordinary Vue named slots are adapted by Vue outlets plus vaporInteropPlugin; raw callbacks do not support manually manufactured VNodes or VDOM return-render functions.

Raw scroll overflowRenderer is evaluated once for a shared fallback pair, and is skipped when both named side slots replace it. Private display:contents carriers share one owner scope: overriding one side detaches that carrier while its resources/reactivity remain owned with the other side; removing the override reinserts the live carrier. Renderer/items pair replacement or component unmount releases the common owner. Detached fallback sides do not have independent unmount semantics.

Native callbacks and real createSlot outlets replace React cloneElement/ref injection. Collapse visibleItem/overflow and scroll visibleItem/overflowStart/overflowEnd use readonly live-getter scopes; each scroll overflow scope.items is its one-dimensional side array. Raw callbacks receive ordinary item/index values and may remount their owned branch when those values change, while keyed native wrappers stay stable.

Collapse uses one item tree and temporary inert hidden candidates, then unmounts folded items. Folded-only closure changes without source, renderer identity, font, container or visible-content changes cannot be observed without mounting that content.

Scroll renders item wrappers as explicit observer targets and owned start/end overflow wrappers. CSS order arranges their visual positions; DOM order and keyboard traversal are not rearranged to imitate React child insertion.

An effective scroll observer batch notifies onVisibleStateChange before onIntersect; the fixed React wrapper notifies onIntersect before its setState completion callback. Observer visibility follows isIntersecting, and an all-invisible batch retains the stable-key overflow cache.

The fixed React width/4 maxCount heuristic is not reproduced. Collapse mounts all candidate items for each required full measurement, uses their actual widths and may converge over several layouts; this O(n) non-virtualized path has no large-list performance guarantee.

Collapse minimums are finite non-negative floored/clamped values; invalid inputs and serialized duplicate keys are rejected. Safe missing/undefined items and default renderers differ from upstream crashes.

The raw scroll overflowRenderer retains the actual upstream two-dimensional [startItems,endItems] input and two-part native return. Native scroll overflowStart/overflowEnd are explicit independent slot outlets rather than one tuple-returning slot, so RC9 owns each side and interop outlet correctly; these are Vapor slot adaptations, not new upstream props, events or expose methods. String/number property paths use the pinned es-toolkit get compatibility; observer keys serialize and numeric/string collisions are rejected.
No new public imperative ref, list role, keyboard or selection protocol. Caller owns semantic content and focus; temporary measurement nodes receive only internal inert/aria-hidden protection.
Existing G10 observers/scheduler and private layout logic replace the upstream React wrappers and Foundation class without expanding the Foundation patch or Tooltip production inline profile.

Vue RC9/vue-jsx RC2 strict independent TSX peer-install rejection remains separate from precompiled consumers. No SSR, hydration, CJS, publication, full pixel-equivalence, other-browser/device or foreign-realm renderer acceptance.

Slot scope properties are shallow readonly live getters and reject replacement/deletion; supplied records and arrays retain caller identity and are not deeply frozen. Read reactive properties inside native JSX effects or conditional blocks; an outer plain JavaScript slot condition does not rerun automatically.

Collapse retains fixed integer clientWidth arithmetic. Root padding contributes to available width, border does not, and external flex gap is not separately deducted. Arbitrary extra gap/margin or subpixel layouts do not have a total-bounding-box no-overflow guarantee. Minimum visible items may intentionally overflow; non-monotonic overflow renderers use finite conservative convergence rather than a promised unique optimum.

mappings.api: Fixed collapse/scroll modes, direction, minimum items, integer measured renderer widths, itemKey, observer threshold, wrapper styles and notifications; real owned Vapor renderers/slots, native attrs and bounded single-tree measurement with explicit safety, ownership and event-order differences.
mappings.types: OverflowItem uses Record<string, unknown>; mode-discriminated Props keep collapse scalar-array and scroll tuple callback signatures. Named collapse slots are visibleItem/overflow; scroll slots are visibleItem/overflowStart/overflowEnd with readonly live-getter scope.items for each side. ReactIntersectionObserverProps and OverflowListState remain internal rather than exposing a fictitious React/Vue instance surface.
mappings.statics: __SemiComponentName__ metadata only; no public static subcomponent or imperative ref. React defaultProps, propTypes and getDerivedStateFromProps are adaptation internals.
mappings.subpaths: browser root and default/named semi-ui-vue/overflowList values/types with paired CSS/SCSS; Node root excludes the component. No legacy React lib/es/lib/cjs mirroring.

families.reviewedDecision: The fixed Avatar and AvatarGroup browser contracts are accepted for native Vapor with owned content, instance registration, image revisions, text geometry and explicit runtime safety. Border custom-style propagation, managed image callback validation and focus cleanup on native-node replacement are verified by regression tests and independent review. Strict declarations, per-source four-dimensional coverage, Chinese documentation, complete browser regression and four isolated tarball consumers passed full local verification. No other public family or additional environment support is accepted.

limitations: Browser native Vapor only; no component SSR, hydration, CJS, publication, full pixel equivalence, other-browser/device or foreign-realm renderer acceptance. Locked Vue RC9/vue-jsx RC2 strict independent TSX installation rejection is distinct from precompiled consumers.

Scalar children is string or number; only string children is measured. Default slots own native rich content and are not inspected, cloned or scaled. Synchronous raw renderers normalize primitives and arrays; async results are rejected. Locked JSX types cannot distinguish every VDOM value statically.

Group registers actual mounted descendant Avatars and orders them by real DOM position. Stable keyed instances stay mounted while folded under hidden/inert/aria-hidden. Non-Avatar slot content is uncounted; nested Groups isolate membership. This differs from React clone/unmount behavior.

Group renderMore receives shallow readonly snapshots of public props, symbol id, DOM index and label, not reusable ReactNode or native Block instances. Renderer replacement can remount its branch; arbitrary conditional JavaScript outside native reactive JSX is not automatically rerun.

Image callbacks use one current-source owner and become inert after source change/unmount; this intentionally avoids upstream duplicate error dispatch. Only synchronous false prevents default fallback. Canonical imgAttr source and error overrides retain documented priority; unsafe HTML/text writes, string event attributes and managed source/event aliases are rejected. Managed imgAttr onLoad/onAbort/onError/onKeydown/onFocus/onBlur retain single-function declarations; null/undefined mean absent and invalid runtime callback types are rejected synchronously.

Measurement uses the fixed integer offsetWidth/gap Foundation formula on the live text tree, plus G10 resize/scheduling and scoped font/mutation resources. Zero dimensions or 2*gap >= width retain the previous scale. Rich content has no automatic fit guarantee.

Fixed maxCount Number/slice arithmetic includes negative, fractional, boxed, NaN and infinite boundaries; unusual counts can differ from the actual folded count. Group forces shape/size and forwards rest to members; its own container has no general attrs API.

Only fixed clickable string/image Enter and Escape behavior is provided; rich slot keyboard semantics belong to the caller. No Avatar.Group, new imperative method, public Image or other public family is introduced.

Top/bottom custom and default content retain preset-size and shape gates. Per-instance SVG IDs use getRandomValues. Existing Foundation patch/inlining, current document/ref/realm and shared-component contracts remain unchanged.

The fixed theme defines overlap z-index rules only for Group member positions 0 through 20, including the default more indicator position; higher positions remain countable and collapsible but have no corresponding ordered z-index rule.

mappings.api: Fixed Avatar defaults, image fallback/error decision, text geometry, size/shape/color, hover/top/bottom/border and Group count/overlap contracts, adapted to single-owner native slots and instance registration with explicit runtime safety and lifecycle differences.
mappings.types: Native AvatarProps/AvatarGroupProps and original shape/size/color aliases are public. ReactNode renderers become synchronous native content; Group restAvatars becomes readonly descriptors. React AvatarState and Foundation AvatarAdapter remain internal, without a fictitious public instance API.
mappings.statics: Avatar retains __SemiComponentName__ and elementType='Avatar'; the fixed source has no Avatar.Group. AvatarGroup has component metadata only and no public imperative methods.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root named Avatar/AvatarGroup and avatar default/named entries, avatar/avatarGroup default/named, CSS/SCSS exports. Node root excludes both. Legacy React lib/es/lib/cjs paths are not mirrored.

families.reviewedDecision: Accepted native Tag, TagGroup and SplitTagGroup with owned native content, fixed close and keyboard behavior, count-based folding and direct DOM split boundaries. Root and subpath Tag-only consumers discard unused Group and Popover implementations; Group consumers retain them. Initial split marker ownership is preserved without inferring later ownership transfer. Strict declarations, actual tarball consumers, source coverage and browser checks pass within the recorded renderer and installation limits.

limitations: Browser native Vapor and separately tested Vue interop are distinct paths; no component SSR, hydration, CJS, publishing, complete pixel equivalence, other-browser/device or foreign-realm renderer acceptance. Locked Vue RC9/vue-jsx RC2 strict independent TSX compiler installation refusal is not replaced by precompiled application consumers.

Tag, TagGroup and SplitTagGroup are independent public values. There are no Tag.Group, Tag.TagGroup or Tag.SplitTagGroup aliases, closeIcon/closeContent/close slot, separator, update:visible, afterClose or new public imperative ref methods. Tag retains __SemiComponentName__ metadata; the fixed family has no TagFoundation class.

Tag children/prefixIcon/suffixIcon use scalar data or synchronous owned content factories. The default native slot has one owner and takes priority. A close callback receives the existing slot function identity when present, not pre-executed child results; callbacks must not execute it to inspect children. Native renderer results are not cloned, inspected, cached or stringified. Locked Vue RC9 VaporRenderResult explicitly includes VNode, so public types also accept some VNode factories that the runtime native-renderer boundary does not support. No VNode detection or conversion is added. Interop default slots remain separate and tested; custom factories must return native content, as verified by a native input factory with owned watchEffect and disposal.

Close stops propagation and immediate propagation before notifying onClose. Only event.defaultPrevented vetoes built-in hiding; callback return values do not. Uncontrolled close adds the fixed invisible class and retains the subtree. Presence of visible, including explicit undefined, is controlled; removing the key keeps the most recent visibility. Resource release requires actual removal/unmount, not CSS hiding.

Fixed keyboard handling belongs to the interactive root div: Enter activates, Delete/Backspace may close before preventDefault and onKeyDown, Escape blurs the event target. The close div adds no separate keyboard stop, Space activation or roving navigation. No automatic next-Tag focus transfer is introduced.

Internal Avatar receives only avatarSrc and avatarShape as src/shape; it adds no Tag avatarAlt/imgAttr/image-event API. Existing Avatar revisions/fallback/resources remain its own contract. Consumers needing explicit image alt or image controls can own an Avatar in custom content.

TagGroup normal data records inherit falsy item size/avatarShape; truthy tagKey precedes scalar children. Missing effective keys use stable record identity instead of per-render random keys, and duplicate effective keys are rejected. Missing tagList is an empty list instead of the upstream map error. Custom items are scalar content or synchronous factories keyed by identity; already-rendered Blocks are not reusable data items.

TagGroup is count-based and does not duplicate OverflowList width/font measurement or G10 scheduling. maxTagCount/restCount preserve numeric arithmetic and slice boundaries, including negative/fractional/NaN/infinite values; non-number values including null are rejected. Callback order is item.onClose then onTagClose; the Group never removes input records and hidden records still count.

TagGroup mode is narrowed to default/custom; the fixed source treats other strings as normal mode. It has no default slot or generic root attrs protocol. Its +N uses owned multi-root content. showPopover reuses Popover ownership, trigger arbitration and cleanup; popoverProps explicitly present content, even undefined, replaces default remainder content. Crossing folded/popup branches can remount content and does not guarantee DOM identity across branches.

SplitTagGroup decorates actual direct Element children with first/last classes and observes native DOM changes, rather than cloning React elements. Text/comments do not count, hidden direct elements do count, fragments and For unfold into real siblings, and nested descendants do not count. Observer/classes must release on unmount; fragment behavior differs from React fragment class injection. Initially present first/last markers remain caller-owned; a later repeated declaration of a component-added marker does not transfer ownership. Ordinary dynamic classes are retained.

Tag defaults snapshot the existing global resolver at instance creation. Runtime safety rejects unsupported callback, enum, list and renderer inputs; safe native attrs do not constitute a general URL/CSS/custom-renderer sanitizer. Existing Foundation patch/inlining, dependency exceptions, current document/ref/realm and all eighteen delivered-family contracts remain unchanged.

Tag default/named, tag/group, tag/splitTagGroup and type-only tag/interface are browser package adaptations. The fixed upstream manifest explicitly exports the legacy tag/group/interface entries but lacks an explicit SplitTagGroup package exports entry; the native split subpath is not claimed as an identical legacy export map.

mappings.api: Fixed Tag color/size/shape/avatar/defaults/visibility/close and keyboard contracts, TagGroup list/callback/count/Popover behavior, and SplitTagGroup direct siblings are mapped to native Vapor-owned content and actual DOM coordination. Tag captures configured defaults per instance; interactive callback identity is compared with that captured default.
mappings.types: Native TagProps, discriminated TagGroupProps, SplitTagGroupProps and the fixed TagColor/TagSize/TagType/TagShape/AvatarShape aliases; ReactNode becomes scalar data or synchronous owned native content. Native event types include KeyboardEvent in close/click and optional tagKey, reflecting actual behavior. TagState and React instance internals remain private.
mappings.statics: Tag retains `__SemiComponentName__`="Tag" only. The fixed source has no Tag.Group, Tag.TagGroup or Tag.SplitTagGroup static public subcomponents; Group and Split are independent exports without new ref methods.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root named Tag/TagGroup/SplitTagGroup; tag default/named/aggregate types, tag/group default/named, tag/splitTagGroup default/named, tag/interface types, and CSS/SCSS style exports. Node root excludes all three component values; legacy lib/es/lib/cjs paths are not mirrored. The split subpath is an explicit native packaging adaptation.

families.reviewedDecision: Native Vapor Badge is accepted after fixed-source API audit, strict source and emitted declarations, ownership and lifecycle regressions, full browser documentation and E2E checks, four isolated tarball consumers, styles and provenance, three Badge DCE modes and independent review. Explicit native slot, renderer realm and peer-install boundaries remain.

limitations: 原生default slot声明存在即锚定，即使其内部当前为空；移除声明才恢复children的truthiness判断。组件不预执行、检查、缓存或克隆slot/VNode。
复杂count/children为同步原生renderer；原始React节点映射为原生factory。VaporRenderResult上游类型包含VNode不表示native factory支持h()；interop宿主default slot由Vue bridge独立管理。
dot关闭自定义数量分支并销毁其内容，再次显示重挂；承载内容的独立owner不因此替换。
不提供公开命令式ref、静态子组件、size、showZero、count slot或自动ARIA/键盘协议。style || countStyle落在内部span。无BadgeFoundation、计时/观察/RAF测量资源。
根浏览器入口只具名Badge值，badge子路径提供default/具名值及类型；Node根仅静态设施。锁定RC9/vue-jsx严格peer安装边界、无SSR/水合/CJS/完整像素等价保持。
原生factory沿用当前Vue renderer realm的Node范围；G10裸DOM跨document能力不等于支持foreign-realm factory、跨document委托事件迁移或任意跨realm组件。
style/countStyle遵循Vue原生CSS赋值，非零长度必须显式单位，不自动补px。原生factory重执行时新建的组件/数组子项可能重挂；DOM保留限于已创建内容内部的更新与稳定key列表，不承诺跨factory调用复用。

mappings.api: 固定count/dot/type/theme/position/overflowCount/style/className/children/countClassName/countStyle及三个mouse回调映射原生Vapor。count与承载children独立；无默认99，0阈值禁截断；默认位置动态继承ConfigProvider direction，显式位置不镜像。
mappings.types: BadgeProps使用原生CSS/HTML属性和MouseEvent；ReactNode映射BadgeContent同步factory，BadgeSlots仅default，类型只在badge子路径公开。保留上游数值边界与安全可表达的类型外计算；不承诺React类型同构。
mappings.statics: 无Badge静态子组件或公开命令式方法；React类实例不映射为Vapor公共代理。
mappings.subpaths: 浏览器root具名Badge；./badge提供default/Badge与类型。固定上游legacy lib/es入口映射为短子路径，不提供其CJS或SSR承诺。

families.reviewedDecision: Accept the reviewed native Typography family with explicit native content ownership, fixed string ellipsis and copy semantics, official numeral formatting, strict browser package surfaces and documented adaptation boundaries. No additional public families or runtime compatibility targets are introduced.

limitations: Browser native Vapor only, with separate ordinary Vue interop. No SSR, hydration, CJS, publication, other-engine/device or complete pixel equivalence. Locked RC9/vue-jsx strict independent compiler peer installation remains unsupported.

Native default slots own their content by declaration presence. Rich content is never probed, cloned, inspected as VNodes or stringified for ellipsis. Synchronous raw renderers have separate primitive normalization; renderer replacement can remount its owned branch.

Ellipsis supports explicit string children. Private measurement recreates component-owned decoration styles and scalar text, never user content. Explicit shallow option values preserve fixed upstream evaluation and errors; non-string rich content does not receive automatic ellipsis.

Numeral uses the exact official formatter. Native rich descendants are formatted explicitly through the scoped format function instead of React DFS/clone. No new Intl, currency or group-separator API. Positive infinite byte-conversion tokens are rejected to prevent the fixed upstream nonterminating loop.

Copying uses the fixed synchronous boolean result and feedback contract. Rich content requires explicit copyable.content; no Promise or public Clipboard component is introduced. Owner-document, Selection restoration and exception cleanup are explicit adaptations. Custom copy renderers do not supply the default operation-ref geometry and may remount when rerun.

Only Typography container forwardRef is a native DOM ref; no child React-class imperative methods. Existing explicit Tooltip ARIA scope/wrapperId and native current-realm renderer limits apply. Stable-key moves preserve node identity but native Vapor can lose focus during DOM relocation; no new focus-restoration protocol is added.

Numeral adds one exact Foundation formatter source; copy adaptation has its own pinned source attribution and MIT. Existing Tooltip eighteen-source closure, Foundation patch, consumer dependency policy and all prior public-family contracts remain independently enforced.

mappings.api: Typography container and the fixed Text/Title/Paragraph/Numeral API are adapted to native owned slots/renderers; scalar ellipsis, copy, formatting, decorations and semantic roots retain audited defaults and explicit boundary differences.
mappings.types: Public aliases map native DOM events, CSS and synchronous renderer ownership; React internal states and nodes do not imply public native instances. Component types live on the typography family or leaf subpaths, not additional root short names.
mappings.statics: Typography.Text, Typography.Title, Typography.Paragraph and Typography.Numeral retain their component identities; no other public static API is introduced.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root Typography; typography default/named; four lower-case leaf default/named entries. Node root excludes the family. Legacy React lib/es/lib/cjs paths are not mirrored.

families.reviewedDecision: The fixed Empty contract is accepted with explicit native slot and synchronous renderer ownership, mount-gated body theme observation, URL/symbol illustration semantics, data-attribute filtering and no default illustration or public imperative API. Source and strict declarations, lifecycle and DOM identity tests, themed Chinese documentation, four isolated tarball consumer flows, tree-shaking and existing-family regressions passed; the implementation and its documented differences were independently reviewed.

limitations: Browser native Vapor and separately tested ordinary Vue interop only. No SSR, hydration, CJS, publication, other-engine/device or full pixel equivalence. The independent strict RC9/vue-jsx compiler peer-installation limitation remains.

No default illustration or Empty Foundation state machine exists upstream. G08 illustration resources are supplied by callers; native URL images and symbol descriptors preserve their fixed semantics. The independent Empty stylesheet includes the fixed Typography styles required by its Title dependency.

Native named/default slots and synchronous native renderers replace ReactNode values. Declaration presence owns each region even when its native output is empty; content is never probed, cloned, cached as VNodes or stringified. Replacing renderer identity may remount its owned branch; keyed DOM movement does not add a focus-restoration protocol.

Only mount-time truthy darkModeImage or a declared darkModeImage slot enables body theme-mode observation; later introduction does not subscribe. Existing observation persists after dark content removal until unmount. No ConfigProvider theme, matchMedia, default image size or new async image handling is added.

Only data-* attributes and the explicit className/style inputs reach the root; class is a Vue alias. No new ARIA live region, role, native event forwarding, keyboard protocol, public ref method or static child is provided. React class implementation methods are not native instance APIs.

Synchronous renderer normalization supports native nodes, fragments, components, arrays and scalar content; raw VNode/Promise/arbitrary object output is unsupported despite the broad upstream VaporRenderResult union. The supported document/realm remains the current browser document.

mappings.api: Empty preserves fixed layout, content truthiness, URL/symbol/custom illustrations, mount-gated body theme observation and root data attributes without a default illustration or additional public family.
mappings.types: EmptyProps and native slot/renderer/image types replace ReactNode and CSS types on ./empty; default slots represent children.
mappings.statics: No static child components or public imperative methods. React class implementation fields are not exposed.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root Empty; ./empty provides default/named Empty and public types. Node root excludes the component; legacy React lib/es/lib/cjs paths are not reproduced.

families.reviewedDecision: Accept the fixed browser Card, CardGroup and Card.Meta contract with native owned slots and synchronous renderers, explicit content truthiness and loading branches, independent actions, the Space-based group and documented entry, ref and environment differences. Strict declarations, full coverage, real browser regressions, four isolated tarball consumers and independent source and visual review support this decision.

limitations: Native slot declaration presence is distinct from visible output; slots are not pre-executed or inspected.
Only browser ESM is targeted. Existing independent TSX compiler peer-installation, current-document and realm, SSR/hydration/CJS and full pixel-equivalence limits remain.
CardGroup is a Space wrapper without child cloning or inherited Card props. No selected, size, layout or imperative Card ref API is introduced.
Loading replaces only the body content through Skeleton; header, cover, actions and footer remain mounted. A declared empty slot is a present content source; no content inspection is performed.

Primitive string titles reuse Typography.Title ellipsis and Tooltip and require an explicit application ARIA ID scope. Native title slots and renderers are not inferred as strings. Boxed String and arbitrary object factories are unsupported.

Actions preserve the upstream index identity and sparse array positions, not an invented business-key API. Stable keyed lists belong to native content or Group slots; node identity and focus during DOM movement are distinct assertions.

Group source default spacing is 16 despite the upstream Chinese table saying 12. It forwards data attributes and private runtime Space align/vertical/wrap values, not general DOM attributes or a new declared Group API.

Card and Meta filter destructive DOM setters and string event handlers while forwarding safe native attributes. Class aliases follow native Vue normalization. Meta creates neither Avatar nor Typography implicitly.

Card isolated CSS/Sass includes its existing Typography, Skeleton, Space and Tooltip closures. Caller-composed Avatar and Button styles remain separate. No new Foundation state machine, patch profile, production runtime dependency or public Image family is introduced.

mappings.api: Fixed Card header priority, raw content truthiness, independent actions and loading branches; CardGroup spacing/grid Space wrapper; Meta content regions.
mappings.types: Native synchronous content and owned slots replace ReactNode. CardGroup retains its narrow public props; runtime Space forwarding is separately documented.
mappings.statics: Card.Meta is the only static child. React class implementation fields and methods are not exposed.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root Card and CardGroup; ./card, ./card/cardGroup and ./card/meta provide explicit component and type entries. Node root remains infrastructure only.

families.reviewedDecision: The browser List and List.Item contract is accepted against the fixed source with explicit native renderer ownership, sparse-input ordering, scoped interop and abnormal loading differences. Source and packed declarations, lifecycle and DOM behavior, themed documentation, four isolated tarball consumer stages, tree-shaking and per-file coverage were individually verified and independently reviewed. List uses the existing Grid, Spin and locale facilities without a List Foundation state machine or another public family.

limitations: Native slot declaration presence is distinct from visible output; slots are not pre-executed or inspected.
Only browser ESM is targeted. Existing strict independent TSX compiler peer-installation, current-document, SSR/hydration/CJS and pixel-equivalence limits remain.
List has no rowKey, Item.Meta, actions or imperative ref methods. Root exposes only List; ListItem is its static child and a leaf subpath value.
Fixed data rendering appends declared children. Native data ownership uses index positions because React child keys cannot be inspected or cloned; stable keyed declarative lists remain caller-owned.

Boolean loading delegates to Spin and preserves content. Truthy invalid runtime loading normalizes to true; unsupported falsy runtime null/0/NaN/empty string values retain Spin behavior and can remain busy with a global Spin.delay > 0. This is an explicit runtime-input difference, not an expanded public boolean type. Empty display uses the existing locale context and an internal div, not public Empty or a List Foundation state machine.
Only data attributes pass through List and Item, with the Vue class alias and explicit fixed mouse callbacks. No automatic roles, live region or keyboard protocol is added.

Normal content accepts synchronous native factories, scalars and sparse arrays. Data renderer native blocks exclude scalar/null/hole leaves. Sparse data is rejected before renderer callbacks, unlike fixed upstream map callback/error ordering; this changes callback side effects for unsupported sparse input. React/VNode results are not inspected or cloned.
The isolated stylesheet includes fixed Grid and Spin closures. No Foundation patch, production inline profile, new dependency or unrelated public family is introduced.

Locked RC9 does not preserve List context for direct h(List) -> VDOM slot h(List.Item). Interop scope is an application-owned native Vapor List/Item wrapper mounted by ordinary Vue, with bridged VDOM content; this does not claim unrestricted component nesting interop.

mappings.api: Fixed List default, data/children append, header/footer/loadMore, locale empty and Spin loading; Item header/main/extra and context mouse callbacks; Grid wraps the native item body.
mappings.types: Native synchronous content and owned slots replace ReactNode. Generic data renderer receives item and index and returns a native block. Internal React ListContextValue is not a public native instance contract.
mappings.statics: List.Item is the only static child. No Meta, state fields or implementation methods are exposed.
mappings.subpaths: Browser root List; ./list default/named and public types; ./list/item default/named ListItem and Item types. Node root remains infrastructure only.
